publicSourceEvidence.modelsDirectory:
SP-API Models

Directory for SP-API models and release notes

The following sections show all Selling Partner APIs (SP-APIs) and indicate whether the API is available for seller or vendor accounts. To identify the APIs, notifications, and reports that you need for specific use cases, refer to SP-API Seller Use Cases and SP-API Vendor Use Cases.

For a complete summary of API updates, refer to SP-API Release Notes. For releases prior to January 19, 2022, refer to Announcements in the Selling Partner API GitHub repository.

For information about API deprecations, refer to the SP-API Deprecation Schedule.

A+ Content Management API

You use the A+ Content Management API to create and edit A+ Content.

Current version	Legacy versions	Availability	Sandbox
2020-11-01 (Reference | Model)	None	Sellers and Vendors	Static
Release notes
Action Items API

You can use the Action Items API to manage tasks for selling partners. When Amazon identifies an action that a selling partner can take, such as a recommendation, an issue to fix, or a task to complete, it publishes an Action Item for you to present to the selling partner in your application.

Current version	Legacy versions	Availability	Sandbox
v2026-06-01 (Reference | Model)	None	Sellers only	Static
Release notes
Action Plans API

Use the Action Plans API to create, configure, and execute action plans from pre-defined templates or custom-built workflows.

Current version	Legacy versions	Availability	Sandbox
v2026-06-01 (Reference | Model)	None	Sellers only	Static
Release notes
Amazon Warehousing and Distribution API

You can use the Amazon Warehousing and Distribution (AWD) API to create and update inbound orders to ship inventory to AWD distribution centers, track inventory inside AWD distribution centers, and track shipments on the way to AWD distribution centers. For information about AWD API operations, data types, and schemas, refer to the Amazon Warehousing and Distribution API Reference.

Current version	Legacy versions	Availability	Sandbox
v2024-05-09 (Reference | Model)	None	Sellers only	Static
Release notes
App Integrations API

You use the App Integrations API to send notifications to Amazon selling partners and display the notifications in Seller Central.

Current version	Legacy versions	Availability	Sandbox
v2024-04-01 (Reference | Model)	None	Sellers only	Static
Release notes
Application Management API

Seller Analytics Dataset Use Case Guide

How to use the Seller Analytics dataset with Data Kiosk.

This guide describes the specifics of the Seller Analytics dataset. For general information about the usage of Data Kiosk, refer to Data Kiosk API.

The seller analytics dataset in Data Kiosk has the following benefits:

Cross-domain analytics: Structure custom queries to access metrics across multiple domains such as sales, traffic, promotions, account health, search, reviews, defects, and returns. You can do this in a single query to explore Selling Partner use cases and address business priorities. Additionally, this dataset allows you to aggregate data at date, ASIN, MSKU, brand, and other granularities in the same query. For example, you can view sales metrics per day, week, or month at ASIN granularity.
Comprehensive metrics: More than 100 metrics across the sales, traffic, promotion, account health, search, reviews, defects, and returns domains.
Multi-store queries: Retrieve data for multiple Amazon stores in a single call, provided all requested stores are in the same region.
Period-over-period benchmarking: Request week-over-week, month-over-month, and year-over-year comparisons alongside the metric values themselves, without issuing a second query for the prior period.
JSONL reports: All reports are returned in a scalable JSON Lines format.
Secure data access: Request visibility is limited to requests submitted by a given application, ensuring security of Selling Partner data.
Access the schema

To access the seller analytics schema, download the schema: analytics_sellerAnalytics_2025_03_31.graphql. You can use any GraphQL tool to explore the schema and build queries. You cannot submit queries from these tools.

To submit the queries and retrieve your custom report, follow the steps in the Data Kiosk Use Case Guide.

The dataset exposes a single view, sellerAnalyticsView, on the analytics_sellerAnalytics_2025_03_31 domain. This one view spans all metric domains.

sellerAnalyticsView takes the following arguments:

Argument	Type	Required	Description
startDate	Date!	Yes	The start date of the data to retrieve. Must be no more than two years ago.
endDate	Date!	Yes	The end date of the data to retrieve. Cannot be in the future.
aggregateBy	DateGranularity!	Yes	DAY, WEEK, or MONTH.
currencyCode	String	No	Currency for all monetary amounts, in ISO 4217 format. Defaults to USD.
marketplaceId	[String!]!	Yes	The Amazon store identifiers to retrieve data for. All identifiers must be in the same region.

The view is available to seller accounts only.

Metric access rights

Access to the seller analytics dataset is governed by the role assigned to your application. Two access levels apply:

Sales and traffic access: Grants the sales, traffic, promotion, account health, search, reviews, defects, and returns metric groups, and the asin, productTitle, msku, brand, brandCode, parentAsin, fulfillmentChannel, productGroup, and marketplaceId group-by attributes.
Sales and lending access: Grants the lending metric group, the sellerAttributes object, and the encryptedMerchantCustomerId group-by attribute, in addition to the fulfillmentChannel and marketplaceId group-by attributes.

Requesting a field your application is not authorized for returns an authorization error rather than a null value. If your application is authorized for a restricted set of Amazon stores, requesting a store outside that set returns Unauthorized marketplace access.

Totals and grouped metrics

sellerAnalyticsView returns two parallel structures over the same metric type:

totals: metric values aggregated across your entire catalog for the time period.
metrics: an array of entries, each with a groupByKey and the metric values for that key.

The following are not supported in totals: the trailing 120-day product defect snapshot metrics listed under accountHealth, criticalReviewRate, returnedRate, and all fields in the defects group. Requesting them there returns The following fields are not supported in totals.

Metric domain-specific behavior

Some metric groups are not additive across time periods, or are not resolved from the same underlying data as the rest of the dataset. This section describes those behaviors.

Snapshot metric behavior

The trailing 120-day product defect metrics in the accountHealth group are snapshots rather than period sums. They represent a state at a point in time and cannot be added across periods.

When a request contains these metrics, additional date restrictions apply:

Daily: The startDate and endDate must be the same date, and that date must be one for which snapshot data exists. If they are not, the error message identifies the valid dates.
Weekly: Eight weeks. This time period includes the current week and the previous seven weeks.
Monthly: 24 months. This time period includes the current month and the previous 23 months.

A query may mix snapshot metrics with ordinary period metrics. When it does, the two sets are resolved separately and merged into one response, so the snapshot restrictions above still apply to the request as a whole.

B2B metric behavior

The B2B metrics (averageSellingPriceB2B, orderedProductSalesB2B, unitsShippedB2B, glanceViewsB2B) are declared in the schema but are not yet served. Requesting one returns The following fields are not yet supported. See Metrics that are not yet available.

Promotion attribute behavior

The following fields in the promotion group describe the promotion itself rather than measuring performance:

promotionStartDate
promotionEndDate
promotionAsinStateType
promotionType
promotionStatus
dealId
dealTitle

These are attributes of the promotion and are not additive across periods.

Search domain behavior

Search metrics are grouped by keyword through queryKeyword rather than through groupByKey. Because a keyword is not a catalog attribute, grouping by it affects which metrics can be returned alongside it. See Column compatibilities.

Defects snapshot behavior

The defects metrics are snapshots computed over a trailing six-month window, not period sums. They represent the state of each product's return defects as of the latest available snapshot and cannot be added across periods. Each product carries one return-defect topic per snapshot; a topic can change from one snapshot to the next as the trailing window moves.

Returns behavior

Returns are attributed to the day the returned unit was shipped, not the day it was returned. Return data is computed with a delay of about 45 days, so:

returnedUnits and totalRefundAmount for the most recent ~45 days may be null or incomplete.
returnedRate may appear artificially low for recent dates, because returned units lag while shipped units are current.
Catalog-only requests

Requests that select only group-by attributes and no metrics are not supported. Such a request returns Catalog requests (i.e. requests containing only GroupBy metrics) are not supported yet. Every query must select at least one metric alongside its groupByKey.

Date behavior

The query outputs automatically adjust the startDate and endDate based on the requested date granularity. Every request is checked to ensure that the requested date is valid. For example, startDate must be in the past, startDate must be before or equal to endDate, and startDate must be no more than two years ago.

Adjustments:

Weekly: The startDate is rolled back to the preceding Sunday and the endDate is rolled back to the preceding Saturday, so that the range covers whole weeks. After adjustment the range must span at least seven days; a narrower range returns an error that identifies the most recent valid week.
Monthly: The startDate is rolled back to the first day of its month. If the endDate is not already the last day of a month, it is rolled back to the last day of the preceding month, so that the range covers whole months.
Daily: No adjustment is applied.
Data availability: The endDate is additionally capped to the most recent date for which all requested metrics have data. If the startDate is later than that date, the request returns an error identifying the latest available date for the requested granularity.
Partial data availability: There are situations where data is available for parts of a time period, but not for the entire time period. This scenario occurs when data is requested within one to two business days. In such cases, the response for periods that are unavailable contains null values.
Benchmarking behavior

Every numeric metric can carry a timeRangeBenchmarking object expressing the percentage change against a prior comparable period. Which comparisons are available depends on aggregateBy:

aggregateBy	Available benchmarks	Comparison period
DAY	None	—
WEEK	weekOverWeek, yearOverYear	The preceding Sunday-to-Saturday week; the same ISO week number in the prior year
MONTH	monthOverMonth, yearOverYear	The preceding calendar month; the same calendar month in the prior year

Requesting a benchmark that is not available for the selected granularity returns Unsupported TimeRangeBenchmarking requested for <granularity> granularity, along with the list of benchmarks that granularity does support. In particular, no benchmarking is available at DAY granularity.

If you do not select any timeRangeBenchmarking subfields, the object is null and no additional work is performed to compute it.

For rate metrics (criticalReviewRate, returnedRate, returnDefectContribution), the benchmark is the difference between the two periods' rates expressed in percentage points, rather than a percentage change.

Column compatibilities

Not every metric can be broken down by every group-by attribute. Compatibility is evaluated per request, against the attributes you selected in groupByKey.

Requesting an incompatible combination is not an error. When a query groups by an attribute and also requests metrics that are not available at that granularity, the request is resolved in parts and merged into a single response. Metrics that cannot be broken down by the requested attribute are returned as null for those rows, rather than being dropped or causing the query to fail.

Practically, this means you should read a null in a grouped row as "this metric is not available at this granularity" rather than as "this metric was zero". If you need to distinguish the two, request the metric in a second query that omits the attribute it is incompatible with.

The one case that does return an error is a set of metrics with no overlapping data availability at all. That returns The requested columns are not compatible together with the list of requested columns.

Rules for query construction

All queries must have at least one group-by field.

All queries must request at least one metric. Group-by attributes alone are not sufficient.

All requested Amazon stores must be in the same region. For example, a single query cannot request data for the US and GB stores.

Requested currency must be one of the supported ISO 4217 codes:

AUD
BRL
CAD
CLP
CNY
COP
EGP
EUR
GBP
INR
JPY
MXN
NGN
PLN
SAR
SEK
SGD
TRY
USD
ZAR

If currencyCode is omitted, amounts are returned in USD.

aggregateBy must be DAY, WEEK, or MONTH.

FAQ
When is data ready?

All metrics in the seller analytics dataset are ready after 34 hours. Data for a given day is generally available at 10 AM local time two days later. For example, data for January 1st is available at 10 AM local time on January 3rd. In the event that data is delayed and unavailable, the response is null for the specific date or dates for which data is unavailable.

Why is a metric null in a grouped row when the same metric returns a value elsewhere?

The metric is not available at the granularity you grouped by. Requesting metrics that are unavailable at a requested granularity does not fail the query; the unavailable metrics are returned as null for those rows. Re-request the metric without the attribute it is incompatible with to get its value. See Column compatibilities.

Can I request a benchmark at daily granularity?

No. Benchmarking is available at WEEK and MONTH granularity only.

Can I query multiple Amazon stores in one request?

Yes, provided all requested stores are in the same region. A request spanning regions returns All requested marketplaces must be in the same region.

Can I retrieve catalog attributes without requesting any metrics?

No. Requests that select only group-by attributes are not supported. Include at least one metric alongside your groupByKey.

Why does returnDefectTopic show only one topic per product?

Each product carries one return-defect topic per snapshot, reflecting the trailing six-month window. The topic can change between snapshots as the window moves.

Shipping API v2 Reference

Provides programmatic access to Amazon Shipping v2 APIs.

Overview

The Amazon Shipping API is designed to support outbound shipping use cases using Amazon Shipping and Amazon Buy Shipping for orders originating on Amazon-owned marketplaces as well as external channels/marketplaces. With these APIs, you can request shipping rates, create shipments, cancel shipments, and track shipments.

Carrier Support: Sellers enrolled in the Fulfilled by Merchant (FBM) Program can use this Shipping API V2 to purchase shipping labels for Amazon Shipping and/or third party shipping carriers like UPS, USPS, FedEx, DHL, etc. Complete list of supported carriers and shipping services can be found on Seller Central.

For Amazon marketplace orders (On-Amazon): Carrier labels for Amazon Shipping and third party carriers are available
For other channels (Off-Amazon) e.g. Merchant website, eBay, Shopify etc: Only Amazon Shipping is available.

To indicate if the label you are purchasing is for On-Amazon or Off-Amazon, use ChannelType.

Operation: purchaseShipment

Description

Note: You must complete the purchase within 10 minutes of rate creation by the shipping service provider for channelType as EXTERNAL which is for OFF-Amazon volume. If you receive this error response, you must get the rates for the shipment again.

Solicitations v1

Send non-critical solicitations to buyers.

With the Solicitations API you can build applications that send non-critical solicitations to buyers. You can get a list of solicitation types that are available for an order that you specify, then call an operation that sends a solicitation to the buyer for that order. Buyers cannot respond to solicitations sent by this API, and these solicitations do not appear in the Messaging section of Seller Central or in the recipient's Message Center. The Solicitations API returns responses that are formed according to the JSON Hypertext Application Language (HAL) standard.

For more information, refer to:

Solicitations API

Support v2025-02-01

You can use the Selling Partner Support API to programmatically retrieve information about a selling partner's Amazon support cases. You can list a selling partner's support cases, retrieve the details and status of a specific case, and review the full history of contacts (email, phone, and chat communications) exchanged with Amazon support, including any scheduled callback appointments and attachments.

Supply Sources v2020-07-01

Manage the configurations and capabilities of seller supply sources.

The Selling Partner API for Supply Sources lets you build and manage the configurations and capabilities of seller supply sources. With this API, sellers can also update information about existing supply sources and provide location level inventory.

Sellers who sell across multiple channels can use this API to publish absolute location-level inventory from their own inventory management systems, including POS, ERP, and WMS.

FBA Inventory API
You use the Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA) Inventory API to retrieve information and track the real-time availability of your inventory in Amazon's fulfillment network at the marketplace level. You can get details such as listing condition and inventory quantities such as:

Fulfillable: Inventory that can be picked, packed, and shipped.
Inbound: Inventory that is on its way to Amazon's fulfillment network.
Reserved: Inventory in Amazon's fulfillment network that is being picked, packed, and shipped; or is sidelined for measurement, sampling, or other internal processes.
Unfulfillable: Inventory that cannot be sold.
Researching: Inventory that is misplaced or warehouse damaged units that are actively being confirmed at an Amazon fulfillment center.

This API is available in all marketplaces.

v1 (Reference | Model)	None	Sellers only	Dynamic

You use the Feeds API to upload data to Amazon to manage your selling business. There are feeds for a wide variety of use cases, such as creating listings, managing inventory and prices, acknowledging orders, and more. Refer to Feed Type Values for a list of available feed types.

The Selling Partner API for Finance Remittance provides programmatic access to vendor payment remittance data. This data includes what Amazon paid or deducted, the invoices each payment covers, and the associated dates and identifiers. It returns the same data available on the Payments > Remittance view in Vendor Central, so you can retrieve your cash flow breakdown, including invoice payments, deductions, vendor returns, and advertising without exporting from Vendor Central manually.

You can also request lists of inbound shipments or inbound shipment items based on criteria you specify. After your inventory has been received in the fulfillment network, Amazon can fulfill your orders regardless of whether you are selling on Amazon's retail website or through other retail channels.

For details about API operations and associated data types and schemas, refer to the Fulfillment Inbound API reference.

v2024-03-20 (Reference | Model)	v0	Sellers only	Static

Listings Restrictions API
You use the Listings Restrictions API to check if there are any restrictions that prevent the creation of a listing for an item in the Amazon catalog. This API supports checking multiple Amazon store IDs for listings restrictions in a single call, and you can optionally filter the restrictions based on condition type. Each Amazon store ID in a request counts as a separate request against the rate limit, but does not affect the cost of the API call. For more information, refer to Listings Restrictions API Rate Limits. If an item is restricted, you might be able to take additional steps to request approval to create a listing. When approval is required, the API returns next step links so you can pursue approval to create the listing. Refer to the Listings Restrictions API Reference for details about API operations and associated data types and schemas.

You can use the Listings Restrictions API in conjunction with the Listings Items API . For example, you can first determine whether listings restrictions exist using the Listings Restrictions API. If no restrictions exist, you can then call the Listings Items API to create offer-only listings. Refer to the Listings Items API Reference for more information about the Listings Items API.
Current version	Legacy versions	Availability	Sandbox
v2021-08-01 (Reference | Model)	None	Sellers only	Static

📘
Note

Current version	Legacy versions	Availability	Sandbox
v2026-04-20 (Reference | Model)	None	Sellers only	Static

Notifications API
You use the Notifications API to subscribe to notifications that are relevant to your selling business. You can create a destination to receive notifications, subscribe to notifications, delete notification subscriptions, and more. Instead of polling for information, your application can receive information directly from Amazon when an event generates a notification to which you are subscribed.

You can subscribe to notifications on behalf of sellers or vendors. To determine whether you can subscribe to a notification type on behalf of sellers only, vendors only, or both, go to notificationType. We allow multiple subscriptions with different payload versions per application, notification type and party (seller/vendor). For supported payload versions of different notification types, refer to notificationType.

🚧
Build a backup mechanism

As a best practice, we recommend that you have a means to retrieve needed information in the event of an unexpected outage or delay in notification delivery.
Current version	Legacy versions	Availability	Sandbox
v1 (Reference | Model)	None	Sellers and Vendors	Static

You use the Product Fees API to retrieve estimated fees for a product. You can then account for those fees in your pricing. You can use the getMyFeesEstimates operation to get product fee estimates for a list of products and marketplaces, and then set prices based on those fee estimates. You must specify your products by ASIN or SKU (not UPC, ISBN, or other identifiers).

You must include an original identifier in each product fees request. This identifier is included in the fees estimate so that you can correlate a fees estimate with an original request.

❗
Important

The estimated fees returned by this API are not guaranteed. Actual fees can vary.
Current version	Legacy versions	Availability	Sandbox
v0 (Reference | Model)	None	Sellers only	Static

Product Pricing API
You use the Product Pricing API to retrieve product pricing and offer information for products in the Amazon catalog. The Product Pricing API is designed to help you develop automated solutions that sellers can use to update and manage their prices. Building in automation for your sellers allows them to react faster to keep their prices competitive and attractive to customers.

⭐
Tip

The Product Pricing API supports the development of repricers. Repricers are automated pricing tools that can continuously monitor price points, competitor prices, and other relevant factors in order to adjust a seller's prices in real-time. Repricers use data and insights from Product Pricing and Notifications APIs to help sellers maintain a competitive price advantage.

officialNotApplicableApis.officialDefinition:
Finance Remittance API
The Selling Partner API for Finance Remittance provides programmatic access to vendor payment remittance data. This data includes what Amazon paid or deducted, the invoices each payment covers, and the associated dates and identifiers. It returns the same data available on the Payments > Remittance view in Vendor Central, so you can retrieve your cash flow breakdown, including invoice payments, deductions, vendor returns, and advertising without exporting from Vendor Central manually.
Current version	Legacy versions	Availability	Sandbox
v2026-03-17 (Reference | Model)	None	Vendors only	Static
Release notes

Invoices API
You use the Invoices API to retrieve invoice data programmatically and streamline your bookkeeping processes. The Invoices API enables you to search for invoices within a specified date range, track invoice payment status, and retrieve detailed line-item information for reconciliation with purchase orders.
Current version	Legacy versions	Availability	Sandbox
v2026-06-25 (Reference | Model)	None	Vendors only	Static
Release notes

Vendor Direct Fulfillment Inventory API
You use the Vendor Direct Fulfillment Inventory API to exchange inventory stock levels with Amazon.

You use the Vendor Direct Fulfillment Orders API to access your direct fulfillment vendor order data. You can receive purchase orders and send order acknowledgments.
